topics.name: Inversion with never, seldom, not only, hardly

options: The whining schoolboy walked slowly to school.
The whined schoolboy walked slowly to school.
The whine schoolboy walked slowly to school.
questions.rule: A boy who is whining is a whining boy. The -ing participle works like an adjective here.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct comparison.
options: The soldier is more braver than the schoolboy.
The soldier is braver than the schoolboy.
The soldier is bravest than the schoolboy.
questions.rule: Comparing two people: braver than. Never use more with an -er word.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: An action used as the subject takes the -ing form (verbal noun): Swimming is good exercise.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: One of the + superlative is followed by a plural noun: one of the greatest writers.

questions.after: wear your helmet on the scooter.
questions.rule: Advice: had better + base verb. You had better wear your helmet.

questions.after: I seen such a huge crowd at a school play.
questions.rule: After Never at the start, the helper verb comes before the subject: Never have I seen.
The participle shining describes the noun faces, so it comes just before it.

chat: Is your grandfather older than your grandmother?
options: Yes, he is three years more old than she is.
Yes, he is three years oldest than she is.
Yes, he is three years older than she is.
questions.rule: Comparing two people: older than. Do not use more or the superlative.

chat: It's getting late. Shall we take a taxi or the bus?
options: I would rather take a taxi tonight.
I would rather to take a taxi tonight.
I would rather taking a taxi tonight.
questions.rule: Would rather is followed by the base verb, without to: would rather take.

questions.source: Old age is the weakest stage of life.
options: Old age is weaker than any other stage of life.
Old age is more weaker than any other stage of life.
Old age is weaker than any other stages of life.
questions.rule: Superlative to comparative: weaker than any other + singular noun.

options: Seldom my grandfather does complain about his age.
Seldom does my grandfather complains about his age.
Seldom does my grandfather complain about his age.
questions.rule: After Seldom, use does + subject + base verb: Seldom does he complain.

options: You had not better shout in the library.
You had better not shout in the library.
You had better not to shout in the library.
questions.rule: Negative advice: had better not + base verb, with no to.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The phrase playing the soldier describes the actor, so use the -ing participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: I have ever seen compares with all plays, so use the superlative: the most interesting.
The children receive the feeling, so use the -ed participle: they were amused by the act.

questions.before: The schoolboy is not as cheerful
questions.rule: Positive degree pattern: as ... as (not as cheerful as).

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that begins with Never.
questions.rule: Never at the start: helper verb + subject + main verb (Never have I seen).

chat: Did you enjoy the play at the theatre yesterday?
options: Yes! Not only was the acting superb, but the music was also lovely.
Yes! Not only the acting was superb, but the music was also lovely.
Yes! Not only was the acting superb, but the music were also lovely.
questions.rule: Not only at the start needs inversion: Not only was the acting superb. Music is singular: was.

questions.prompt: Join the sentences using a participle.
questions.source: The schoolboy picked up his satchel. He walked slowly to school.
options: Picked up his satchel, the schoolboy walked slowly to school.
Picking up his satchel, walked the schoolboy slowly to school.
Picking up his satchel, the schoolboy walked slowly to school.
questions.rule: The first action becomes an -ing phrase: Picking up his satchel, the schoolboy walked...

questions.source: The soldier is braver than the lover.
options: The lover is not as braver as the soldier.
The lover is not as brave as the soldier.
The lover is not so brave than the soldier.
questions.rule: Comparative to positive: not as brave as. The base adjective goes between as ... as.

options: Having finished his homework, Rohan went out to play.
Having finish his homework, Rohan went out to play.
Have finished his homework, Rohan went out to play.
questions.rule: A completed earlier action: Having + past participle (Having finished).

options: I would rather walk than take the bus.
I would rather to walk than take the bus.
I would rather walk than to take the bus.
questions.rule: would rather + base verb + than + base verb: rather walk than take.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Would rather takes the base verb for every subject: she would rather stay.

questions.before: Hardly had the curtain gone up
questions.rule: The pair is Hardly ... when. (No sooner goes with than.)
Comparative form of a superlative: higher than any other + singular noun.
Comparative pattern: more famous than. Few actors were more famous than Shakespeare.

chat: Why is Arjun looking so tired today?
options: He was exhausting after cycle ten kilometres.
He was exhausted after cycled ten kilometres.
He was exhausted after cycling ten kilometres.
questions.rule: A person who feels tired is exhausted. After a preposition, use the -ing form: after cycling.

chat: Is life today easier than it was in my time?
options: Yes, it is much easier in many ways.
Yes, it is very easier in many ways.
Yes, it is more easier in many ways.
questions.rule: Make a comparative stronger with much, not very or more: much easier.

questions.source: I have never seen such a fine actor.
options: Never I have seen such a fine actor.
Never have I seen such a fine actor.
Never have I saw such a fine actor.
questions.rule: Never at the start: have I seen. Keep the past participle seen.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: than needs the comparative: more colourful. An action at the same time: left the hall feeling happy.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: You had better leave now, didn't you?
You had better leave now, won't you?
You had better leave now, hadn't you?
questions.rule: had better uses the helper had, so the tag is hadn't you?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The plays were written by him, so describe them with the past participle: plays written by Shakespeare.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Only two girls are compared, so use the comparative: the taller girl.

questions.after: my grandparents miss the evening news.
questions.rule: Inversion after Seldom; the subject grandparents is plural, so do + base verb miss.
The participle broken describes the window; was repaired is the passive verb.

chat: Shall I book the tickets for Saturday's show?
options: You'd better book them today, Papa. They sell out fast.
You'd better to book them today, Papa. They sell out fast.
You'd better booked them today, Papa. They sell out fast.
questions.rule: You'd better (= you had better) + base verb: you'd better book.

chat: How is your batting practice going this month?
options: Never I have worked so hard, Sir!
Never have I worked so hard, Sir!
Never have I work so hard, Sir!
questions.rule: Never at the start: have I worked. Present perfect = have + past participle.

questions.source: The old man lost his teeth, and he also lost his eyesight.
options: Not only the old man lost his teeth, but he also lost his eyesight.
Not only did the old man lose his teeth, but he also lost his eyesight.
Not only did the old man lost his teeth, but he also lost his eyesight.
questions.rule: Not only did + subject + base verb (lose), then but ... also.

questions.source: Very few writers are as famous as Shakespeare.
options: Shakespeare is one of the most famous writer.
Shakespeare is one of the famousest writers.
Shakespeare is one of the most famous writers.
questions.rule: Very few ... as ... as becomes one of the most + plural noun.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: would rather read than watch (base verbs). Habit with he: waters, like goes.

options: Only after the curtain fell did the actors take a bow.
Only after the curtain fell the actors took a bow.
Only after the curtain fell did the actors took a bow.
questions.rule: Only after ... at the start needs inversion in the main clause: did the actors take.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Perfect participle = Having + past participle: Having seen (not saw).

questions.before: It is late, and the roads are flooded; you had better
questions.rule: had better is always followed by the base verb: had better stay.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence that begins with Seldom.
questions.rule: Seldom + does + subject + base verb. aching is a participle describing knees.

chat: Was the second half of the match as exciting as the first?
options: No, it was far less exciting than the first.
No, it was far lesser exciting than the first.
No, it was far less exciting as the first.
questions.rule: Comparative of exciting going down: less exciting than. Lesser is not used before adjectives.

questions.source: Shakespeare is the greatest dramatist in the world.
options: No other dramatist in the world is as great as Shakespeare.
No other dramatist in the world is as greater as Shakespeare.
No other dramatists in the world is as great as Shakespeare.
questions.rule: Superlative to positive: No other + singular noun + as great as.

questions.source: As soon as the actor entered, the audience cheered.
options: No sooner had the actor entered when the audience cheered.
No sooner did the actor enter than the audience cheered.
No sooner the actor entered than the audience cheered.
questions.rule: No sooner did + subject + base verb ... than. No sooner never pairs with when.

questions.rule: have I seen; Having rehearsed (having + past participle); a baby who cries is a crying infant.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Of all = superlative: the most carefree. would rather remember. A person who feels the thrill is excited.

questions.rule: burst out crying; a person who feels fear is scared of something; had better + base verb: leave.
